title: Horizontal toggle clamp
summary: four-bar toggle, over-centre stop, closed loop
description: A horizontal hold-down toggle clamp of the M6, 900 N class: a formed base in two mirrored L halves held by the pivot rivets, a formed U-bar with an M6 spindle and rubber cap, a stamped link and handle with a red PVC grip, all on rivet pivots.
process: Laser cutting and press forming, zinc plating, riveting, spot welding, PVC dipping

difficulty.rationale: One closed four-bar, but four real sheet parts with a joggle, flat patterns, own-frame configurations and an independent closed form over the motion.

materials: Low-carbon steel, press-formed, bright zinc plated (base, U-bar, link, handle)
Steel rivets and M6 spindle, zinc plated

motion.cycle: there and back: open, through the toggle line, to the stop just past it, and open again

contacts.why: the upper lock nut is tightened against the top of the bar
the lower lock nut is tightened against the underside of the bar
the thread is the joint: the nut's bore is the tap drill and the rod is at the major diameter (F-014)
the thread is the joint: the nut's bore is the tap drill and the rod is at the major diameter (F-014)
the rubber cap presses the workpiece: it touches at the stop and compresses by a few hundredths of a millimetre passing the toggle line (the clamping preload)

prompt_test.model: Claude Sonnet 5.5, medium effort, through craft3d-cli
prompt_test.result: Passed every Acceptance line on the numbers: 0 dof, knee 3.0000° past the toggle line, cap at the block, every fit 0.15 mm, bar 90.99° at handle 40.99°, advantage 20.90 against its closed form to 0.0005 %. It guessed the reference frame and where the reach is measured from; the prompt now states them. About 400 commands in 55 CLI calls.
